status: final judgement against complete frozen isolated measurements; prices and savings remain estimates
score_rule: sum of positive isolated bound savings per deduplicated program group, weighted by execution context, times generality divided by burden. Savings already include static occurrences; do not multiply by occurrences again.
deduplication: For each candidate family and count_group choose the largest positive isolated saving among variants/frontends; report all individual rows separately. This is a conservative alternative envelope, not a composed overlay.

bn254_fp_multiply.rationale: Generic254-bit reduction supports Groth16/BitVM arithmetic; new prime/reduction proof.
bn254_fp_multiply.tier_reason: The measured base- and extension-field kernels show substantial local savings and a plausible BitVM proof path. Benchmark canonical input and output conversion before valuing a pairing verifier; only the dense multiplication component is modeled.

secp256k1_ecdsa_verify.rationale: Known-key external signatures; existing group/scalar lemmas, new ECDSA equivalence.
secp256k1_ecdsa_verify.tier_reason: Known-key ECDSA can reuse existing curve proofs. The corpus separates client signatures and native predicates, and the current price omits two scalar multiplications and range/control work. Benchmark exact affine and scalar checks first.

ecrecover.rationale: Ethereum-address identities; recovery uniqueness, affine encoding and Keccak proofs.
ecrecover.tier_reason: The Ethereum-style bridge, permit and oracle paths benefit. In the quorum example the combined estimate with Keccak fits where either candidate alone does not. Benchmark reusable recovery to a point plus a separate permutation before fixing the Ethereum address and failure ABI.

m31_mul.rationale: Small Mersenne-field multiplication with bounded folding proof.
m31_mul.tier_reason: The full STARK accounts for most savings, and the isolated M31 overlay does not make it fit the fixed-stack scenario. Benchmark this small reusable primitive alongside QM31 because the proof burden is smaller; compare the overlapping savings and exact raw-word contract.

qm31_mul.rationale: Reusable degree4 extension multiplication; field-tower reduction proof.
qm31_mul.tier_reason: The full STARK crosses the fixed-stack scenario by 5,001.074 WU at this estimated price. Benchmark the extension multiply and exact input domain; the margin is conditional and M31 savings overlap.

keccak_f1600.rationale: Reusable permutation across Ethereum commitments, bridge messages and SHAKE; new permutation proof.
keccak_f1600.tier_reason: One permutation matches 12 distinct groups and changes fixed-stack fit in 11 budget-applicable programs. FairSwap falls from 93,362.551 to 1,343.255 WU at the estimate. Benchmark the reusable permutation for hash, bridge, permit, oracle and compressed asset paths before bundling address recovery.

blake3_compress_cv.rationale: Reusable BLAKE3 chaining and 256-bit root output; new seven-round schedule and feed-forward proof over established word operations.
blake3_compress_cv.tier_reason: The bounded BitVM-style tree-hash component has substantial savings but remains one use family. Benchmark the raw CV/first-output-block ABI and compare it with smaller round helpers before proposing a jet.

blake2s_compress.rationale: General32-bit compression; add/xor/rotate composition, new round proof.
blake2s_compress.tier_reason: The exact fixed final-block frontend only matches its own kernel and shares one counting group with BLAKE2b. Broader rounds or common G helpers need a distinct exact reference and new evidence.

blake2b_compress.rationale: General64-bit compression; add/xor/rotate composition, new round proof.
blake2b_compress.tier_reason: The fixed twelve-round final-block prototype matches its own kernel. It does not cover the Ethereum variable-round/final-flag ABI; the current corpus does not justify prioritizing this specialized arrow.

sha256_wots_chain_16.rationale: Generic bounded tweaked SHA256 chain, reusing compression correctness.
sha256_wots_chain_16.tier_reason: Prioritize the fixed-prefix frontend: both stateless variants cross their fixed-stack scenarios and share one counting group. The separate stateful group uses the generic frontend; its overlay prices the observed 18-byte buffer, and the unrestricted 30-compression path needs a separate price.

sha256_wots_chain_16_fixed.rationale: Fixed-address frontend of the same tweaked SHA256 chain family; no extra family credit.
sha256_wots_chain_16_fixed.tier_reason: Prioritize the fixed-prefix frontend: both stateless variants cross their fixed-stack scenarios and share one counting group. The separate stateful group uses the generic frontend; its overlay prices the observed 18-byte buffer, and the unrestricted 30-compression path needs a separate price.

sha256_pair.rationale: General two-block SHA256 helper; existing compression and padding proof patterns.
sha256_pair.tier_reason: A simple Merkle helper has several direct matches and a reusable proof path. Compare its smaller savings and the full verifier residual with existing two-compression composition before adding a separate fixed-size jet.

pubkey_unpack_neg.rationale: General canonical Schnorr key decode; range and field-negation proof.
pubkey_unpack_neg.tier_reason: A cheap parser primitive with small isolated savings in variable-key CSFS. Existing complete Schnorr jets hide the parser in many other entries, so benchmark the paired parser use before prioritizing.

signature_unpack.rationale: General canonical Schnorr signature decode; field/scalar range proofs.
signature_unpack.tier_reason: A small field/scalar range proof is attractive, but direct measured demand is concentrated in variable-message CSFS. Compare shared range checks and full Schnorr verification before selecting the frontend.

div_mod_256.rationale: Wide integer division across fixed-point/state accounting; total zero-divisor convention needs exact proof.
div_mod_256.tier_reason: The estimate crosses the fixed-stack scenario for bounded Uniswap V3 (22,235.642 to 9,708.540 WU against 12,694) and LMSR (17,404.636 to 16,082.774 WU against 16,379). It also materially reduces Balancer and Pendle. Benchmark exact full-width and normalized narrow division separately: the limb proxy is incomplete.

multiply_128.rationale: General wide product with reusable limb carry proof.
multiply_128.tier_reason: This small carry proof has exact matches across 18 groups. The isolated estimate crosses the LMSR scenario by only 191.272 WU; larger savings in some pool predicates leave substantial residuals. Benchmark it against composition from existing Multiply64.

multiply_256.rationale: General wide product with expanded limb carry proof.
multiply_256.tier_reason: The regular wide product matches ten groups; the largest savings are concentrated in Ed25519 and P-256, which remain above their fixed-stack scenarios. Compare generic limb arithmetic against dedicated reductions before selecting a width.

div_mod_512.rationale: Large division and quotient/remainder proof; wide state and zero-divisor convention.
div_mod_512.tier_reason: The bounded Curve invariant still costs 38,396.334 WU against its 5,206-WU scenario; the full StableSwap pool has no exact match. The only fit change is in the BN254 Fp2 kernel. Benchmark unrestricted and normalized division separately; the 512-by-256 price proxy is incomplete.

ripemd160_compress.rationale: Bitcoin HASH160 interoperability; new dual-lane compression proof.
ripemd160_compress.tier_reason: Several Bitcoin HASH160 and interoperability paths match the same compression. Verify whether a compression jet changes spend fit often enough to justify the new dual-lane proof alongside the broader SHA candidates.

sha512_compress.rationale: General hash/HMAC/Ed25519 workload;64-bit SHA2 schedule proof.
sha512_compress.tier_reason: The estimate brings the native BIP32 withdrawal below its fixed-stack scenario. The same compression is useful in HMAC, Ed25519 and BIP47 client work, which is reported separately. Benchmark the reusable block primitive.

p256_fe_multiply.rationale: Non-native curve arithmetic; P256 Solinas reduction proof and canonical field contract.
p256_fe_multiply.tier_reason: Dedicated reduction saves 9,233,450.936 WU in each of the two P-256-based predicates. Residual estimates of 826,747.503 WU for standalone verification and 829,907.725 WU for WebAuthn still exceed their 13,272- and 19,725-WU fixed-stack scenarios. Benchmark the field ABI and compare a reusable curve-level verifier.

ed25519_fe_multiply.rationale: Non-native curve arithmetic;25519 reduction proof and canonical field contract.
ed25519_fe_multiply.tier_reason: Large savings in one interoperability verifier still leave a substantial residual. Benchmark raw field reduction and compare the dedicated curve and SHA-512 pieces before pursuing this as a broadly demanded jet.

koalabear_add.rationale: Exact32-bit wrap-add/single-subtract helper in published/deployed KoalaBear16 Poseidon2, with total noncanonical-word semantics. C needs add/subtract/select; existing32-bit carry/borrow proof patterns apply. Current demand is one component family, not a new full application.
koalabear_add.tier_reason: The exact wrap-and-reduce helper gives a meaningful saving in one deployed-source Poseidon2 component and has a small proof burden. More application evidence is needed before prioritizing a prime-specific add.
